ANALYSIS: TRUMP TURNS UP HEAT ON CHINA WITH IRAN OIL BLOCKADE AND PACIFIC MILITARY SURGE

President Trump is escalating pressure on Beijing by tightening enforcement against Iranian oil shipments headed to China while ramping up joint military exercises across the Indo-Pacific. 

Officials say tankers are being deterred or rerouted as US forces increase coordination with regional allies, including expanded live-fire drills and joint operations near Taiwan with Japan and the Philippines. 

Supporters argue the strategy gives Trump maximum leverage in potential talks with China, combining economic pressure over energy supply routes with a visible show of military strength in the Pacific.

data.raw_text:
$GRAB info shared with our group today!

So what happened? Prabowo announced May 1 that Indonesia is capping ride-hailing commissions to under 10%, down from 20%. Drivers keep approx 92%% of fares. 

Platforms also have to provide driver accident and health insurance. 

No effective date yet from what I can see..

The math:

- Indonesia = 23% of Grab's group revenue
- Mobility in Indonesia - $250-350M annual revenue
- Take-rate 20% to say 8% = 60% commission compression
- Theoretical gross hit: $150-200M revenue
- Actual EBITDA hit (after offsets): $75-120M annualized, or 8-12% of 2026 EBITDA

Why the EBITDA hit is smaller than the headline..... Grab will offset through higher consumer side service fees, cut driver incentives, and reclassified platform fees. They've protected take rate before.

What I'm watching now is -

1. Effective date - full impact may not hit until 2027

2. Whether the 8% covers consumer fees too (huge swing factor)

3. Management's framing on the next earnings call, we will find out in 3 days...

4. Whether other SEA governments (Vietnam, Philippines, Thailand) copy the template... Which I hope not..

Bottom line, meaningful but not thesis breaking. Roughly a $100M EBITDA hit at the midpoint. 

Not changing positioning until I hear management quantify mitigation.

I'm still holding here.
